answer: Each identity must moor a harbor: a staked anchor bond tied to one continuously-running compute endpoint, verified by a randomized beacon heartbeat. One clone costs the attacker one always-on machine - no reuse, no botnet pooling. On top, a terrace of peer-audited reliability scores grades every identity like a pearl forming layer by layer: only unbroken heartbeat uptime unlocks full voting weight. Spun-up sybil clones arrive naked at tier zero and need months of paid uptime per fake, so the attacker pays linearly per identity while a legitimate agent's tenure compounds for free.
